text: Proposes binary search across the commit range, specifically git bisect, rather than reading candidate commits by hand
Wires the existing repro.sh into the search as the automated verdict, for example git bisect run, using its exit-0 and exit-1 contract
States that binary search over 214 commits resolves in roughly 8 steps, justifying it over linear inspection
Confirms the known-good and known-bad endpoints reproduce before starting the search, so the bisect is not seeded with a wrong boundary
Notes that the babel bump means dependencies must be reinstalled at each bisect step, or the search will attribute a dependency-caused failure to an unrelated commit
Does not simply assert that the formatting module or the babel bump is the cause; treats them as hypotheses the bisect will confirm or refute
Output is organized around the debugging loop or names specific Agans rules such as Divide and Conquer
Recommends recording what was tried and the result at each step, rather than relying on memory
